key_insight: MS-TTRL separates correctness verification from generation frequency, resolving the conflict between favoring common answers and preserving rare valid solutions.
engineering_relevance: For reasoning tasks with multiple valid solutions, MS-TTRL enables test-time adaptation without labeled answers while encouraging broader solution recovery.
method: Use Outcome-Level Self-Verification to estimate correctness independently of generation frequency.
Reuse verification through a Three-State Outcome Cache and handle ambiguous outcomes with a Candidate State.
Apply Confidence-Gated Inverse Probability Scaling to strengthen learning from rare, reliably verified outcomes.
evidence_signal: Across two benchmarks, four tasks, three backbone models, and five random seeds per evaluation, MS-TTRL improved Recovery Rate by an average of 19.13 percentage points over the best-performing label-free baseline and approached supervised IPS-GRPO.
watch_item: Rare-outcome reinforcement depends on reliable self-verification; incorrect confidence estimates could amplify invalid solutions.
paper_title: MS-TTRL: Breaking the Frequency Conflict in Multiple-Solution Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
